title: <link> media="", type="", etc. changes are underspecified and contradictory
body:
This is part of the long journey to improve the specification of `<link>` elements, largely by transitioning from shared declarative statements (e.g. "[Processing the media attribute](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#processing-the-media-attribute)" and "[Processing the type attribute](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#processing-the-type-attribute)") to per-type processing models with appropriately factored-out steps.

The "Processing the media attribute" section [says](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#processing-the-media-attribute)

> However, if the link is an external resource link, then the media attribute is prescriptive. The user agent must apply the external resource when the media attribute's value matches the environment and the other relevant conditions apply, and must not apply it otherwise.

But then link types icon, manifest (as of #6444), and stylesheet have their own normative text. Stylesheet is notably different from the others, as it delegates to CSSOM by creating a live reference to the media attribute which CSSOM handles. Icon and manifest are both UA-triggered, and so use a somewhat wishy-washy text such as

> If multiple icons are provided, the user agent must select the most appropriate icon according to the type, media, and sizes attributes. If there are multiple equally appropriate icons, user agents must use the last one declared in tree order at the time that the user agent collected the list of icons.

which could be better by, e.g., specifying whether this impacts fetching or "application".

Then we have others, like modulepreload and resource hints (dns-prefetch, etc.) which have no normative text about the media attribute. So in theory the general "Processing the media attribute" section would apply to those, but I bet in practice that's not implemented.

Similar issues affect the "Processing the type attribute" section, although that's especially delicate for stylesheets.

The ideal end state, IMO, would be:

- Manifest and icon have normative algorithms for collecting all links, picking the best one by checking their attributes against properties of the UA (such as supported image types) or document (language, media), and then fetching that one.
  - The UA can trigger this algorithm at any time.
  - Maybe we suggest or require UAs re-trigger it whenever relevant document features like language or media change
- We investigate modulepreload and resource hints to see if any implementations take `media`, `type`, etc. into account. If so, we update their fetch algorithms and "appropriate times" algorithms as necessary.
- We figure out how type="" works with stylesheet links and incorporate that into the fetching algorithm. This might be blocked on https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/968.
- We delete the "Processing the media attribute" and "Processing the type attribute" sections, incorporating any accurate and useful information and examples they have into the definitions of those attributes. Such information would be changed to statements of fact about how they impact the processing models defined for each link rel.

/cc @domfarolino @zcorpan
